title: Properness from valuation extensions starting in a dense open
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Give spaces the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For morphisms of spaces, separated means that the representable diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]; quasi-compact means that for every affine scheme $T$ and every map $T\to Y$ to the target of a morphism $f:Z\to Y$, the algebraic space $Z\times_YT$ has quasi-compact underlying point space (every open cover has a finite subcover); quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. Locally of finite type and locally of finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type; finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and locally of finite presentation. Proper means separated, of finite type, and universally closed, where universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (agreeing with the scheme convention [def-weil-proper-morphism]). Let $p:H\to X$ be a separated finite-type morphism of algebraic spaces, and let $h:V\hookrightarrow H$ be a quasi-compact open immersion with dense image in the atlas topology. Open immersion means representable with an open immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-open-immersion]. Suppose the following extension property holds. For every valuation ring $R$ [def-trf-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$ [def-weil-field], every map $v:\operatorname{Spec}K\to V$, and every map $x:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ with $p h v=x|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$, there are an injective local homomorphism of valuation rings $R\to R'$ (so $\mathfrak m_{R'}\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$), its fraction-field extension $K\to K'$, and a map $z:\operatorname{Spec}R'\to H$ whose composite to $X$ is the pullback of $x$ and whose restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}K'$ is the pullback of $h v$. Then $p$ is proper. No Noetherian, rank-one, discreteness, or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 089G (lemma-refined-valuative-criterion-universally-closed), conditions (1)--(4), specialized to a quasi-compact dense open and separated finite-type p; uniqueness is supplied by the closed diagonal (Tag 03KU, lemma-separated-implies-valuative, proved by the closed equalizer on a valuation domain).

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary valuation diagram $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to H$, $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ for $p$, without assuming that $\eta$ factors through $V$. The hypothesis on $h$ is quasi-compactness on affine scheme tests, exactly as required by the stacked-valuation node. Apply the stacked-valuation configuration to obtain $C,\mathfrak q,D,L,E,F,b,\alpha,u$ and the four stated compatibility equations. In particular $D=C_{\mathfrak q}$, $E=C/\mathfrak q$ dominates $A$, the generic map of $\alpha$ is $hu$, and the closed restriction of $\alpha$ is $\eta_F$. This is a point-moving input with no lifting hypothesis; it does not assert properness.

source.place: Tag 089G, proof up to the definition of C

proof.text: Apply the hypothesis of the item to the valuation ring $C$ with fraction field $L$, the map $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to V$, and $b:\operatorname{Spec}C\to X$. The required generic compatibility is $p h u=b|_{\operatorname{Spec}L}$, obtained by restricting $p\alpha=bj_D$. We obtain an injective local map $C\to C_1$, fraction field $L_1$, and $z:\operatorname{Spec}C_1\to H$ over $b$ with generic map $(hu)_{L_1}$. These are exactly the hypotheses supplied, with no need to descend this lift to $C$.

As a $C$-module, $C_1$ is torsion-free: for $0\ne c\in C$, injectivity makes its image nonzero in the domain $C_1$, so $c x=0$ implies $x=0$. The torsion-free valuation-module lemma gives flatness. Locality gives $\mathfrak m_C C_1\subseteq\mathfrak m_{C_1}\ne C_1$, and $C$ has only the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_C$ (its nonunits form an ideal: for two nonunits divisibility comparability writes one as a multiple of the other, so their sum is a nonunit), so the flat maximal-ideal criterion gives faithful flatness. Surjectivity on prime spectra then gives a prime $\mathfrak q_1\subset C_1$ with inverse image $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 089G, prime lifting; Tag 0539 (more-algebra-lemma-valuation-ring-torsion-free-flat), Tag 00HP (algebra-lemma-ff), Tag 00HQ (algebra-lemma-ff-rings)

proof.text: Put $D_1=(C_1)_{\mathfrak q_1}$ and $E_1=C_1/\mathfrak q_1$. Both are valuation domains. Indeed any pair of nonzero elements in a valuation domain is comparable for divisibility; this passes to a prime quotient, and to a localization by putting two fractions over a common denominator. Comparability is the valuation criterion for their fraction fields. Since $\mathfrak q_1\cap C=\mathfrak q$, the fraction map $D\to D_1$ is injective and local: $c/s$ maps into $\mathfrak q_1D_1$ exactly when $c\in\mathfrak q$. The induced map $E\to E_1$ is injective, and it is local since $\mathfrak m_{C_1}\cap C=\mathfrak m_C$. Thus $E_1$ dominates $E$ and hence $A$. Its fraction field $F_1$ is the residue field of $D_1$, and the ring maps induce $K\hookrightarrow F\hookrightarrow F_1$.

source.place: Tag 089G, localizations and prime quotients; Tag 088Y (algebra-lemma-make-valuation-rings)

proof.text: Compare the two maps $\operatorname{Spec}D_1\to H$ given by $z|_{\operatorname{Spec}D_1}$ and $\alpha\operatorname{Spec}(D\to D_1)$. Their composites to $X$ coincide by $pz=b\operatorname{Spec}(C\to C_1)$ and $p\alpha=bj_D$, and their generic restrictions both equal $(hu)_{L_1}$. Their equalizer is the pullback of $\Delta_{H/X}$ along this pair. By the separatedness hypothesis, this scheme test of the diagonal is a closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}D_1$. The generic point factors through $Z$. Apply the closed-factorization lemma with $Y=\operatorname{Spec}D_1$ and $g=\mathrm{id}$: the identity factors through $Z$, so the two maps are equal. The cited factorization lemma concerns schemes, exactly as needed for this equalizer, despite $H$ and $X$ being spaces.

source.place: Tag 089G, uniqueness comparison; Tag 03KU (lemma-separated-implies-valuative), closed equalizer proof

proof.text: Restrict $z$ along $\operatorname{Spec}E_1\to\operatorname{Spec}C_1$ and call the result $w$. Its composite with $p$ is $a\operatorname{Spec}(A\to E_1)$: the map $C\to E_1$ factors through $E=C/\mathfrak q$, so use $bi_E=a\operatorname{Spec}(A\to E)$. Restrict the equality of the preceding step to the residue field $F_1$ of $D_1$. The left side is $w|_{\operatorname{Spec}F_1}$, since $C_1\to F_1$ factors through $E_1$. The right side is the pullback of $\alpha|_{\operatorname{Spec}F}=\eta_F$. Thus $w|_{\operatorname{Spec}F_1}=\eta_{F_1}$. Together with the injective local map $A\to E_1$ this supplies the extended lift for the original arbitrary diagram.

The arbitrary diagram of step 1 therefore admits a lift after an extension of valuation rings. Finite type of $p$ includes quasi-compactness on every affine scheme test by the corrected definition in the statement, so the extended valuative existence criterion applies and makes $p$ universally closed. The assumed separatedness and finite type, together with universal closedness, are precisely properness as defined in the statement. No rank, discreteness, Noetherian, or finite-presentation restriction has been used.
